claims.statement: Poland's Office of Electronic Communications reported 67,060 self-service postal kiosks at the end of 2025, up 29.7% from 2024.
The same official report says Poland handled nearly 1.40bn courier items in 2025, an increase of 14.3% year over year.
Hypothesis: despite the large installed base, operators still pay for screened micro-locations controlled by short host options; current operator criteria and fees are unvalidated.

contrary_evidence: A 67,060-unit installed base and 29.7% annual expansion demonstrate a crowded land-grab as much as they demonstrate operator demand.
Postal-market volume growth does not prove that operators will pay intermediaries or that the founder's reachable sites fill network gaps.

economics.acquisition_route: Collect 50 permissioned host submissions in one city, secure at most 15 short conditional options, and obtain written operator site criteria before offering packets.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated path: 1,500 annual activations at PLN 4,000 average net revenue would create PLN 6m revenue; at 25% operating profit and a 4x value, an 80% founder stake is PLN 4.8m, requiring more than PLN 0.2m of previously distributed personal cash to exceed PLN 5m without double counting. A 6-8 year route would require national operator contracts and roughly 2% of the 2025 installed-base scale in annual activations.
economics.founder_time: 8-14 hours per week for scoring, option administration and operator feedback; local verification can be contracted per site.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated estimate: 65-80% after site verification, local travel, mapping, documentation and channel commissions; failed-site screening must remain mostly remote.
economics.payback: Unvalidated target: 9-18 months after 15-30 activations, depending on bounty size and remote-screen rejection rate.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: PLN 2,000-6,000 operator activation fee plus 10-20% of first-year host rent or a fixed renewal administration fee; no host is charged before an operator pays.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hosts may renew leases and introduce other sites; operators repeatedly buy only if acceptance rates and data quality beat direct sourcing.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: micro-geographic host density and a record of activation outcomes improve site ranking, while exclusive option windows stop duplicated speculative submissions
fingerprint.customer: parcel and courier operators expanding or relocating locker networks, with retail, SME and residential property owners as hosts
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: renewable installers, property managers, retail associations and local accountants surface hosts; operator acquisition is centralized through business-development agreements
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: host consent, site imagery, access and power facts, catchment score, conditional option and multi-operator matching sold per activated site with optional renewal administration
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the operator pays a diligence or activation bounty when it accepts and activates a site; the host may share a defined portion of first-year rent after lease execution
fingerprint.problem_trigger: an operator seeks a specific underserved catchment or a host wants recurring rent and footfall without sourcing every operator independently

founder_fit: Low-capital rights origination can start around Wielkopolska through existing business relationships.
Geospatial scoring and workflow automation fit the founder's analytical style.
Local verification and host onboarding can be delegated once scripts and criteria stabilize.
Does not require personal-camera content or inventory ownership.
risks: Poland already has a very large and fast-growing locker footprint, so attractive sites may be saturated.
Operators can source hosts directly and may refuse intermediary fees.
Hosts may lack title, landlord, community, power or planning authority.
Poorly drafted exclusivity could frustrate hosts without creating transferable value.

structure.control_point: a geographically dense inventory of time-limited exclusive host-site options with standardized access, power, title and consent diligence
structure.critical_dependency: operators must still need the micro-location and the host must be able to grant a compliant lease with feasible power, access and local approvals

thesis: Turn underused frontage and parking space at SMEs, housing communities and renewable-installation customer sites into standardized parcel-locker site packets. A host grants a short, no-build exclusive option conditional on title, power, planning, neighbor and operator approval; the service screens catchment and access, then offers the packet to multiple postal operators under pre-agreed rules. Earn only on operator diligence or activation, and never suggest the option is a permit or guaranteed lease.
title: Conditional Parcel-Locker Host-Site Exchange
uncertainties: Which operators pay external activation bounties and what are their current site criteria?
Do hosts value multi-operator matching enough to grant a short exclusive option?
Which micro-markets remain under-served despite national locker growth?
Can site rejection be predicted accurately enough to preserve high gross margin?
